**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

Section 12 of the agreement satisfies the WARRANTY rule at the **preferred** position on its material terms:

- **Period:** conformance-to-Specifications warranty runs for the acceptance period *plus* one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, and continues for as long as the Software stays under Maintenance Services — exceeds the preferred 12 months.
- **Remedy:** § 10(c) requires Garman to repair non-conforming Software at no additional charge; §§ 7–8 give Sparkling rejection with a full refund of all amounts paid during the acceptance period. § 15 preserves direct damages.
- **Disclaimer:** none. There is no "AS IS" or implied-warranty disclaimer anywhere in the document, so nothing erodes the express warranty — a favourable position for us that should not be disturbed.

Sub-elements short of the model language, noted for the file but not flagged: no separate "professional and workmanlike" warranty for installation/conversion/training services, no compliance-with-laws warranty, no no-malicious-code warranty, and the repair duty is qualified as "best efforts." These are worth raising only if the negotiation reopens Section 12 for other reasons.
